profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal design review at an ML audio research lab for a proposal to revisit Masked Conditional Neural Networks (MCLNN) as a lightweight baseline for automatic sound event recognition. The team is preparing a short workshop paper and a reusable internal benchmark recipe comparing an MCLNN implementation against modern compact CNN baselines on ESC-10 and ESC-50. The agenda is to review whether the current design is sufficiently faithful to the original MCLNN paper, whether the experimental plan is 'ready' for execution, and what changes are needed before the proposal is approved. The expected outcome is a go/no-go decision on the proposed replication-and-extension plan, plus agreement on any revisions to the evaluation package and ablation scope.

members.name: Dr. Lena Ortiz
members.expertise: Audio representation learning, efficient neural architectures, empirical study design
members.background: Lena leads a small line of work on lightweight models for on-device acoustic scene and event recognition, and has recently been pushing for historically important architectures to be re-evaluated under modern tooling.
members.private_state: She wants the design review to end with approval so the team can start experiments this week and still make the workshop deadline; she is comfortable with a historically informed but not perfectly archival reproduction as long as the comparison is informative and publishable.
hidden_assumptions: A 'reproduction' is successful if the core inductive bias of MCLNN is preserved, even if the spectrogram extraction and training stack are updated to the lab's current audio template.
'Ready for ablations' means there is enough evidence from a single clean pilot run to justify scheduling the full experiment matrix, not that every reporting standard is already satisfied.
When people refer to the lab's 'baseline frontend,' they mean the default audio preprocessing module currently checked into the shared sound-events benchmark repo.
'Without augmentation' excludes explicit sample-mixing and waveform perturbation, but not lightweight training-time masking used as regularization.

members.name: Kai Menon
members.expertise: Experiment infrastructure, reproducibility, benchmarking pipelines for audio ML
members.background: Kai maintains the group's evaluation framework for audio datasets and is usually responsible for turning research proposals into stable, repeatable runs that can be handed to interns or used in future benchmark reports.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid approving a plan that will later need to be re-run because the implementation is not faithful enough or the reporting artifacts are too thin for the lab's reproducibility standards.
hidden_assumptions: A 'reproduction' should match the original paper's preprocessing and training setup closely enough that any performance difference can be attributed to the model rather than the pipeline.

'Ready for ablations' means the reporting scaffold is already statistically defensible, including multiple seeds and variance reporting, because otherwise the downstream table format will have to change.
When people mention the 'baseline frontend,' they are referring to the audio feature recipe used in the lab's last published environmental-sound benchmark, not merely the current default codepath.
'Without augmentation' means no training-time transformations that alter spectrogram content at all, including time masking or frequency masking.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a faithful reproduction
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say they want a 'faithful reproduction' of the MCLNN baseline.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means preserving the architectural idea of conditional masking over temporal windows while using the lab's modern log-mel extraction, normalization, and trainer defaults.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means reproducing the original paper closely enough in preprocessing and training details that the result functions as an archival-style baseline.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both view themselves as being careful and non-sloppy, and 'faithful reproduction' sounds like an uncontroversial shared goal in a design review, so neither feels a need to unpack whether fidelity is conceptual or procedural.

misalignment_points.topic: What 'ready for the ablation table' requires
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both talk about getting the setup 'ready for the ablation table' before greenlighting the study.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks a single-seed pilot with expected directional behavior is enough to lock the design and launch the full sweep later.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks the design is only ready once the table schema can be populated with multi-seed results and basic variability estimates, so that no review-stage decision is based on unstable numbers.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In research meetings, 'ready' often compresses several stages into one phrase, and both participants assume the other shares their lab habit for what level of evidence is implied before approval.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to reusing 'the baseline frontend' to save time.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the current shared repo's default frontend: 64-bin log-mel features with per-clip normalization and the standard window/hop from the internal benchmark template.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the frontend from the lab's previous environmental-sound paper: the older published recipe with slightly different mel-bin count and dataset-level normalization that he informally calls the baseline frontend.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both frontends are internal standards with overlapping names, both have been called 'the baseline' in recent months, and because the discussion is about design approval rather than implementation minutiae, the ambiguous reference passes unnoticed.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the proposal should stay 'without augmentation' to remain comparable to the original MCLNN claim.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this only rules out explicit data augmentation pipelines such as pitch shift, noise injection, mixup, or external sample expansion, while still allowing light spectrogram masking as a regularizer.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes it rules out any training-time transformation that changes the observed input, including SpecAugment-style time/frequency masking.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are trying to honor the same historical comparison and neither expects the other to interpret 'augmentation' differently because the surface intent—keeping the comparison clean—sounds fully aligned.

turns.inner_thought: I want this approved today so we can start runs this week and still hit the workshop timeline. For me, a faithful reproduction just means the MCLNN idea is preserved: the conditional masking over temporal windows, the lightweight setup, and the historical comparison. I do not need an archival recreation of every preprocessing or trainer detail if we keep the architecture's core inductive bias intact and use the lab's current stack.
